title.value: VideoNavQA: Bridging the Gap between Visual and Embodied Question Answering
title.justification: The title reflects the central theme and aim of the research paper, which is to present the VideoNavQA dataset that evaluates the capability of video and question answering in an embodied environment.
title.quote: VideoNavQA: Bridging the Gap between Visual and Embodied Question Answering

analysis.description: The research paper introduces the VideoNavQA dataset aimed at evaluating video question answering capabilities in nearly-optimal navigation paths within a rich 3D environment. The paper highlights the challenges of the Embodied Question Answering (EQA) task and evaluates various models adapted from Visual Question Answering (VQA) techniques to understand how well current methods perform in this setting.

type.justification: The paper provides empirical evaluations through experiments on the VideoNavQA dataset using different models adapted from Visual Question Answering techniques.
type.quote: We evaluate all of the models described in the previous section on the VideoNavQA task and produce an initial expectation of the feasibility of EQA, using accuracy to compare the overall performance between different architectures.

name.justification: The primary focus of the research is on Visual Question Answering within a 3D environment, assessing how well models perform on answering visual and navigational questions.
name.quote: We investigate several models, adapted from popular VQA methods, on this new benchmark.

name.justification: The paper addresses Embodied Question Answering by providing a task variant focusing on visual reasoning while removing navigation concerns.
name.quote: Embodied Question Answering (EQA) is a recently proposed task, where an agent is placed in a rich 3D environment and must act based solely on its egocentric input to answer a given question.

name.justification: LSTM is used and compared in the experiments to evaluate its effectiveness as a language model within the dataset.
name.quote: The LSTM proves to be the most powerful language model, achieving 7.5% more than the bag-of-words.

is_contributed.justification: LSTM is a well-known model used for comparison in the experiments rather than being a novel contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: The LSTM proves to be the most powerful language model...

is_executed.justification: The LSTM model was executed as part of the experimental evaluation on the VideoNavQA task.
is_executed.quote: We evaluate all of the models described in the previous section on the VideoNavQA task.

is_compared.justification: The performance of LSTM is compared with other models in the experiments.
is_compared.quote: The LSTM proves to be the most powerful language model, achieving 7.5% more than the bag-of-words.

referenced_paper_title.quote: Sepp Hochreiter and Jürgen Schmidhuber. Long short-term memory. Neural computation, 9(8):1735–1780, 1997.

name.justification: The MAC model is adapted for temporal visual reasoning in VideoNavQA tasks, reflecting its use in compositional attention across visual frames.
name.quote: MAC Compositional Attention Networks (MAC) [14] have achieved excellent performance in several VQA tasks [4, 14, 15]. Here we adapt this by applying a MAC model after a 2D-CNN and integrating it over time using an LSTM.

is_contributed.justification: The MAC model is adapted from existing work and is not a novel contribution in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: MAC Compositional Attention Networks (MAC) [14] have achieved excellent performance in several VQA tasks [4, 14, 15].

is_executed.justification: The MAC model was executed as part of the experimental evaluation within the VideoNavQA framework.
is_executed.quote: Here we adapt this by applying a MAC model after a 2D-CNN and integrating it over time using an LSTM.

is_compared.justification: The performance of the MAC model is part of the comparative analysis reported in the experiments.
is_compared.quote: MAC surpasses all other models when identifying colors, with Concat-CNNs achieving the next best result.

name.justification: FiLM is used in extended form to incorporate temporal dimension in the VideoNavQA task, highlighting its contribution to visual reasoning.
name.quote: Here, we extend FiLM to address the additional VideoNavQA temporal dimension.

is_contributed.justification: The FiLM model is an extension of existing work for the task rather than being a newly developed model in the paper.
is_contributed.quote: Feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) [27] has previously achieved state-of-the-art results on visual question answering tasks.

is_executed.justification: The FiLM model was executed in the experimental setup to evaluate its performance on the dataset.
is_executed.quote: Based on single-modality baseline results, we integrate the LSTM model with each of the two vision models, in order to derive a joint representation of the obtained features.

is_compared.justification: FiLM's performance is compared against other models, demonstrating its impact on various question categories.
is_compared.quote: FiLM GP has an edge over others, whereas identifying object types seems to be the hardest task.

name.justification: Concat-CNN3D is used as one of the integration models that combines features extracted by CNNs and language models.
name.quote: Concatenation models: Based on single-modality baseline results, we integrate the LSTM model with each of the two vision models, in order to derive a joint representation of the obtained features. We achieve this by concatenating the final question representation with their respective video representations (Concat-CNN2D/3D).

is_contributed.justification: Concat-CNN3D is developed and adapted specifically for the VideoNavQA task combining video and question inputs.

is_compared.quote: Overall, these results suggest that the models presented manage to exploit the visual context of the environment, improving by a significant margin over the language-only capabilities of the LSTM and BoW.
